Cambodia is implementing ongoing reforms under the Public Financial Management Reform Program (PFMRP), currently framed around Phase 4 (2025–2027). A major reform area is the continued modernization and integration of public financial management information systems. Current implementation includes FMIS-related strengthening and interoperability across core MEF systems and linked sector/subnational systems, including i-PIM, PPP-PIMS, DI-PIMS, PPDMS, SNA-PIMS, BPS, SARMIS, DMFAS, NRMIS, and other budget, cash management, general ledger, inventory, debt, asset, and public investment databases.

Implementation status: ongoing. The reform focus is on system interfacing within the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), across ministries, and with external public-sector entities. A central milestone already achieved is identification/operation of multiple specialized digital systems and the move toward structured interoperability among them. Another milestone is the establishment of Phase 4 of PFMRP and the design of a central integration approach through i-PIM.

Timelines: PFMRP Phase 4 is identified for 2025–2027. A 2023 consultation draft shows the reform agenda was already under preparation by October 2023.

Milestones achieved: development/use of core PFM platforms; formal recognition of system modules such as General Ledger, Cash Management, Inventory Management, debt management (DMFAS), non-tax revenue management (NRMIS), state asset registry (SARMIS), and public investment databases; planning for intra-ministry, inter-ministry, and external system interfacing.

Milestones to achieve: fuller interoperability among MEF systems and with line ministries/agencies; continued technical development of i-PIM as a central data integration platform; improved coordination of business processes for public investment and broader PFM decision-making.

Responsible agencies: Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); General Secretariat of the PFM reform; General Department of Public Financial Management Information Technology (GDPFMIT); General Department of Digital Economy; General Department of Policy; General Department of International Cooperation and Debt Management; General Department of Public-Private Partnerships; General Department of Sub-National Administration Finance; and linked institutions such as the Ministry of Planning.

Donor partners: the PFMRP website identifies development partners including the EU, JICA, and UNICEF.
answers.r: The retrieved documents clearly indicate that Cambodia has active PFM reforms underway, especially digitalization and system integration under PFMRP Phase 4 (2025–2027). The text provides enough detail to draft an open response covering status, timeline, milestones, agencies, and some donor references. The answer avoids inventing specifics not in the extracts, especially where donor support is not linked to a precise reform component.

answers.a:
Cambodia is continuing to implement and expand its Integrated Financial Management Information System (FMIS/IFMIS) as part of the Public Financial Management Reform Program. Implementation is already underway and being rolled out in phases, moving from central/national government operations toward wider use in subnational administrations. Current reform efforts focus on: (1) expanding FMIS usage across ministries and provinces, (2) strengthening change management and user readiness, and (3) deepening interoperability with other government digital systems.

Implementation status: FMIS is operational and being progressively expanded. Recent implementation updates indicate that, since phase 1, FMIS has been deployed at 311 sites, with 8 system functions/modules in operation, 16 external system interfaces, 66 reports generated from the system, and 3,798 users. In addition, FMIS Portal version 1 is being used at 1,870 sites by 3,372 users.

Timelines: The reform is ongoing. The 2023 PFM reform consultation material sets out the reform architecture and implementation responsibilities, while a March 2026 government update confirms continued rollout, awareness-raising, and preparation for fuller use by both existing and new entities.

Milestones achieved: phased rollout launched; adoption by hundreds of sites; active use by thousands of users; operational reporting; and integration work with other systems, including DMFAS (debt management), NRMIS (non-tax revenue), ASYCUDA/e-Customs, banking/EFT arrangements, payroll-related systems, and EFMS in the Ministry of Education.

Milestones to achieve: further expansion to subnational levels, fuller use by newly onboarded entities, continued change-management support, and broader/interoperable integration across intra-ministry, inter-ministry, and external systems.

Responsible agency: The Ministry of Economy and Finance leads implementation through the FMIS Project Management Working Group and relevant MEF units, including the General Department of Public Financial Management Information Technology. Ministries, institutions, and subnational administrations also have implementation, monitoring, and change-agent roles.

Donor partners: Not clearly specified in the retrieved sources.
answers.r: The answer synthesizes Cambodia-specific FMIS reform information from the retrieved sources: the 2023 MEF draft reform document provides the formal reform framework, responsibilities, and planned integration architecture, while 2026 government/related sources confirm ongoing implementation, awareness building, and concrete rollout milestones. Donor partners were not named in the retrieved material, so they are reported as unspecified.
